questions.stem: How do root hair cells absorb water from the soil?

options.text: By osmosis, from the dilute soil solution to the more concentrated cell sap

questions.explanation: Root hair cells absorb water from the soil by osmosis. The soil solution is more dilute (higher water potential) than the cell sap, so water moves into the cell down the water potential gradient.

questions.stem: Why do root hair cells have a large surface area?

options.text: To increase the rate of water and mineral absorption from the soil

questions.explanation: The long, thin extension of root hair cells greatly increases the surface area in contact with soil particles and soil water, maximising the rate of water and mineral absorption.

questions.stem: How do mineral ions enter root hair cells?

options.text: By active transport, using energy from respiration

questions.explanation: Mineral ions are usually at a lower concentration in the soil than in the root cells, so they must be absorbed by active transport, which requires energy from respiration.

questions.stem: Once water is inside the root, how does it move to the xylem?

options.text: From cell to cell by osmosis, across the cortex to the xylem

questions.explanation: Water moves from cell to cell across the root cortex by osmosis, moving from higher water potential to lower water potential, until it reaches the xylem vessels in the centre of the root.

questions.stem: Why do root hair cells have many mitochondria?

options.text: To produce ATP for active transport of mineral ions

questions.explanation: Root hair cells contain many mitochondria because active transport of mineral ions against their concentration gradient requires a large supply of ATP from aerobic respiration.

questions.stem: What would happen to mineral absorption if a root was deprived of oxygen?

options.text: It would decrease because aerobic respiration cannot occur, reducing ATP production for active transport
The root would absorb more water instead

questions.explanation: Without oxygen, aerobic respiration cannot occur and ATP production is greatly reduced. Since mineral ion absorption depends on active transport powered by ATP, mineral uptake would decrease significantly.

questions.stem: What is the Casparian strip in the root?

options.text: A waterproof band in the endodermis that forces water through cell membranes

questions.explanation: The Casparian strip is a waterproof (waxy) band in the walls of endodermis cells in the root. It forces water to pass through cell membranes rather than between cells, allowing the plant to control what enters the xylem.
